exam: What are the key clinical features that differentiate an uncomplicated incisional hernia from a strangulated one? — Sudden pain, vomiting, irreducibility, systemic signs.
In a low‑resource setting, which imaging modality would you use to confirm a hernia and why? — Portable ultrasound: bedside, no radiation, shows contents.
Why is mesh repair contraindicated in a dirty wound? — Risk of infection and mesh failure.

What perioperative antibiotic would you choose for a patient with HIV undergoing hernia repair? — A broad‑spectrum agent covering skin flora and opportunistic organisms, e.g., amoxicillin‑clavulanate.
How would you counsel a patient on preventing recurrence after hernia repair? — Weight control, smoking cessation, avoid heavy lifting, proper wound care.
When is urgent surgery indicated for an incisional hernia? — Signs of strangulation: sudden pain, vomiting, fever, tachycardia.
ai.title: Incisional Ventral Hernia
ai.subject: Surgery
ai.summary: A defect in the abdominal wall after surgery that allows intra‑abdominal contents to protrude. It presents with a palpable bulge, pain, and risk of incarceration or strangulation. Management balances surgical repair against resource limits.

b: Risk higher with dirty wounds, malnutrition, HIV
sections.p: An incisional ventral hernia is a defect in the linea alba or rectus sheath that occurs after abdominal incision. It is common after emergency laparotomies, caesarean sections, or trauma repairs, especially where wound care is suboptimal.

t.b: A reducible, non‑tender bulge suggests uncomplicated hernia; a tender, irreducible bulge raises suspicion of incarceration
Shows bowel loops or fluid; useful in resource‑poor settings

b: Complications: incarceration, strangulation, bowel obstruction, sepsis
